problem: Suppose that $L$ is a linear differential operator such that $L({y}_{1})=3x-5$ and $L({y}_{2})=(x-3)^{2}$ for some functions ${y}_{1}(x)$ and ${y}_{2}(x).$ What is $L(2{y}_{1}+{y}_{2})?$

feedback.problem: Suppose that $L$ is a linear differential operator such that $L({y}_{1})=2-{sin}^{2}⁡x$ and $L({y}_{2})=3{cos}^{2}⁡x$ for some functions ${y}_{1}(x)$ and ${y}_{2}(x).$ What is $L(3{y}_{1}-{y}_{2})?$
feedback.worked_solution:
For any linear differential operator,

$$
L(a{y}_{1}(x)+b{y}_{2}(x))=aL({y}_{1}(x))+bL({y}_{2}(x))
$$

where $a$ and $b$ are constants. 

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}L(3{y}_{1}-{y}_{2}) & =3L({y}_{1})-L({y}_{2}) \\  & =3\cdot (2-{sin}^{2}⁡x)-3{cos}^{2}⁡x \\  & =6-3{sin}^{2}⁡x-3{cos}^{2}⁡x \\  & =6-3({sin}^{2}⁡x+{cos}^{2}⁡x) \\  & =6-3 \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$
